title: Module test B2.2 · Attribution and certainty

blocks.text: Module test B2.2 · Attribution and certainty
Instructions

Week 207 of the calendar, after verification of B2-07 → B2-12INT-04 and INT-05 (and, for varieties, of EGY-14, EGY-15 and ARZ-01; EGY-16 and ARZ-02 are in progress and do not enter the test). Duration: approx. 120 minutes for parts A/E, plus 15 minutes of interview with the tutor. Work without notes; the dictionary by root is allowed only in part D (translation). Fix it with the solution. Part B scripts are at the beginning of solutions: make them read to another person (the song 3 to an Egyptian speaker) or use vocal synthesis for songs in fuṣḥā, without reading them. The text of Part A is without vowels.

rows: Reading: a service with a reference interview, different weight sources, opinions and a verification
Listening: a radio interview, a commentary, a street interview in Egyptian
Language: speech reported, mode, concession, connotation, humanitarian vocabulary, Arabic
Translation from Arabic to English (Rubrication of Accuracy)

If you do not pass the test, review the weaker unit during B2-13 and repeat the tutor test within the week 209. Reading speed (does not enter the score). Before answering the questions in part A, read the text once silently with the stopwatch and note the time: the text has about 340 words. Objective at this point of the course: 85 words per minute (90 at the end of the level).

E · Written production (8 points)

Write an article of opinion in Arabic (230–260 words) on the thesis: "Public museums should be free on the first Sunday of each month" (you can support or reject it). Compulsory elements: title · introduction · explicit arguments · two different subjects (B2-10), one of which with an invented data attributed to a source with the appropriate verb (B2-08) · an objection lodged with ⁧قَدْ يُقَالُ إِنَّ⁩ or ⁧يَرَى البَعْضُ أَنَّ⁩ and a refutation · a concession with ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ … o ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ... · at least two expressions of certainty of different degrees (B2-09) · a conclusion with proposal · no fallacy (B2-10). Evaluation: Accuracy 1–4 + Organisation and argumentation 1–4. Each missing mandatory item removes 1 Point to Accuracy (minimum 1); an obvious fallacy removes 1 I'm on the subject.
F · Oral production (8 points)
With the tutor, about 15 minutes.
1. Interview (5 minutes). Interview the tutor, who interprets a (invented) manager of a public project.

Ask open, precise and in-depth questions; The tutor deliberately avoids a question, and you need to notice and reformulate it. Then report in Arabic, in a minute, what he said and what he did not say (B2-07, B2-08).
2. Discussion (5 minutes). The tutor reads a short opinion text (invented) with an opinion disguised as
Done and a fallacy. Individual, then discuss the thesis with arguments and a concession (B2-10 → B2-12).
3. Egyptian (5 minutes). The tutor interprets an Egyptian passerby in a street interview on a daily theme:

ask at least four questions (open, example, hypothetical, rewording) (EGY-14). Finally, the tutor tells you a little trouble: answer with a suitable proverb and a joke (EGY-15). Evaluation: Accuracy 1–4 + Fluidity and interaction 1–4. The task 3 is part of both criteria. Part F assesses the tutor; Without tutors, it remains unfinished.
